purpose: Set static MSVC C-runtime linkage for both shipped Windows architectures.
behavior: Adds -C target-feature=+crt-static for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.
Comments tie the setting to H5/WP-H and the package verifier's PE import-table check.
contracts: Cargo must run from the Omni directory so this configuration is discovered; a RUSTFLAGS environment value replaces these flags.
dependencies: native/omni/scripts/ci.mjs and workflows supply the Cargo working directory.
failures_or_limits: This config alone does not prove that produced binaries omit VCRUNTIME140.dll; no build was run.

evidence.quote:
# H5 (WP-H): the Windows binaries (the addon and the supervisor) link the C runtime statically, so they need no Visual
# C++ Redistributable (VCRUNTIME140.dll) on the user's machine. `bindings/node/npm/verify.mjs` checks the import table.
# Cargo reads this file when it runs from this directory (scripts/ci.mjs, the workflows); a RUSTFLAGS variable would
# replace these flags.
[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-feature=+crt-static"]

[target.aarch64-pc-windows-msvc]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-feature=+crt-static"]

purpose: Define the mirror's three-OS CI gate and release-mode selection.
behavior: Runs only for v* tag pushes or manual workflow_dispatch; the manual request supplies release and test_filter.
Uses Ubuntu 24.04, macOS 14 and Windows 2022 with Node 22, fail-fast disabled, a 40-minute limit and per-ref cancellation.
RELEASE becomes 1 for v tags or a true manual release input; Linux release runs install the musl target and Linux always relaxes the user-namespace AppArmor restriction.
contracts: Contents permission is read-only; cache saves only on refs/heads/main.
All jobs execute node scripts/ci.mjs; TEST_FILTER is passed through the environment.
dependencies: External GitHub Actions and Linux sysctl are execution dependencies.
failures_or_limits: The comment still names packages/omni whereas this baseline is native/omni.
A workflow definition is not an observed CI result.

evidence.quote:
strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-14, windows-2022]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 40
    env:
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
      RELEASE: ${{ (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || inputs.release) && '1' || '' }}
      TEST_FILTER: ${{ inputs.test_filter }}

- name: Rust toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rustup show active-toolchain || rustup toolchain install
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ] && [ -n "$RELEASE" ]; then rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; fi
      # One cache per OS and lockfile. Only main saves it (a run by hand on main), so tags read it without filling the quota.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - name: Linux PID-reuse test needs unprivileged user namespaces
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
      - run: node scripts/ci.mjs

purpose: Build and verify installable npm tarballs for all eight platform packages.
behavior: Manual-only workflow has GNU/musl Linux x64/arm64, Darwin x64/arm64 and MSVC Windows x64/arm64 rows; fail-fast is off and each has 40 minutes.
GNU Linux installs Zig and cargo-zigbuild; musl builds in Alpine; Windows bootstraps rustup if absent.
Builds with build-artifacts.mjs, packs the selected platform, then clean-installs on Node/Bun/Deno except musl, which checks Node and Bun inside node:22-alpine.
Uploads dist/tarballs/*.tgz and errors when no files exist.
contracts: Contents permission is read-only; package publication is explicitly a separate manual lead action requiring the owner's consent.
Non-Alpine cache reuse is read-only; Bun 1 and Deno 2 runners are selected through npx.
dependencies: GitHub runner images, Docker, Zig and rustup.
failures_or_limits: No release job or installation proof was executed in this analysis.

evidence.quote:
- name: Build (${{ matrix.build }})
        shell: bash
        run: node scripts/build-artifacts.mjs ${{ matrix.id }}
      - name: Pack
        shell: bash
        run: node bindings/node/npm/pack.mjs dist ${{ matrix.id }}
      - name: Clean install and run (${{ matrix.runtimes }})
        if: matrix.build != 'alpine'
        shell: bash
        run: for rt in ${{ matrix.runtimes }}; do node bindings/node/npm/verify.mjs dist/tarballs $rt; done
      # musl: the proof runs under Alpine (node:22-alpine), with npm and Bun's musl build; Deno has no musl build.
      - name: Clean install and run on Alpine (${{ matrix.runtimes }})
        if: matrix.build == 'alpine'
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w -e HUGR_BUN node:22-alpine sh -euc '
            apk add --no-cache git tar >/dev/null
            for rt in ${{ matrix.runtimes }}; do node bindings/node/npm/verify.mjs dist/tarballs $rt; done'
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: npm-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: dist/tarballs/*.tgz

purpose: Build the private Rust Node-API cdylib backing the JavaScript package.
behavior: Names the library hugr_omni_node, emits only cdylib, and disables Rust test/doctest harnesses because Node-API symbols resolve from the host.
Inherits package version, edition, Rust requirement, license, repository and lints from the workspace.
Depends on the local hugr-omni core, napi 3 without default features and with napi8, napi-derive 3 and build-time napi-build 2.
contracts: publish=false reserves npm packaging for W14.
The comment excludes napi tokio_rt and an async-runtime SPI because the core owns the runtime; Node/Bun/Deno tests are the intended host proof.
failures_or_limits: Dependency ranges alone do not prove host compatibility; Cargo.lock records actual resolutions.

evidence.quote:
publish = false # npm packaging is W14's (ADR-0004)

[lib]
name = "hugr_omni_node"
crate-type = ["cdylib"]
# The addon resolves the Node-API symbols from the host process at load time, so it only links as a cdylib: a test
# harness of it would not link. Its proof is the TS suite (`bindings/node/test`), run on Node, Bun and Deno.
test = false
doctest = false

[dependencies]
hugr-omni = { path = "../../crates/hugr-omni" }
# ADR-0004: Node-API 8 (Node 22+, Bun, Deno); no `tokio_rt` (the core owns the one tokio runtime), no async-runtime SPI.
napi = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = ["napi8"] }
napi-derive = "3"

[build-dependencies]
napi-build = "2"
